136945.etyen:
A lexicalized use of the calendar date 17. mai (“17 May”), read aloud as syttende mai (“the seventeenth of May”).
The date refers to 17 May 1814 at Eidsvoll. The Norwegian Constitution had been unanimously adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 16 May; on the following day it was dated and signed by the presidency, and Prince Christian Frederik was elected king of an independent Norway. The date consequently became a symbol of the Constitution and of Norwegian political independence.

1005041.etyen:
From drøvtygge (“to ruminate, chew the cud; to rehash”) + -eri (“action/activity-forming noun suffix, often pejorative”). The base verb drøvtygge (“to ruminate, chew the cud”) contains drøv (“cud”), of uncertain origin, and tygge (“to chew”). The latter is from Old Norse tyggja (“to chew”) and tyggva, from Proto-Germanic *kewwaną (“to chew”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ǵyewh₁- (“to chew”). The suffix -eri (“action/activity-forming noun suffix”) is from Low German -erie; Bokmålsordboka describes it as originally a merger of Greek -ία (-ía) and Latin -arius.
Compare Danish drøvtyggeri
